scope: Primary sources for hydrogen flammability, ignition, jet dilution and flame radiation; storms, updrafts and lightning are committed project products (CM1 ring; atmospheric electricity via the joint synthesis).

sources.citation: Coward, H. F. and Jones, G. W. (1952). Limits of flammability of gases and vapors. US Bureau of Mines Bulletin 503.
sources.access: Full text (OCR of the UNT scan) read by a verification agent.
sources.use: Dry gases, upward propagation in a 4-inch tube: hydrogen in air 4.0-75.0% (p. 16); upper-limit mixtures hold 5.2-5.3% O2; no H2-N2-air mixture propagates flame below 4.9% O2 (p. 20). Saturated gas: 4.1/74 upward, 9.0/74 downward.
sources.limit: Laboratory tubes and vessels at room conditions.

sources.citation: Zabetakis, M. G. (1965). Flammability characteristics of combustible gases and vapors. US Bureau of Mines Bulletin 627.
sources.access: Full text read by a verification agent (UNT catalogue lists wrong authors; the title page says Zabetakis).
sources.use: Table 21: hydrogen in air 4.0-75% at 25 C, 1 atm; Fig. 111: minimum O2 5.0% with N2 as the added inert.

sources.citation: Ono, R. and Oda, T. (2008). Spark ignition of hydrogen-air mixture. Journal of Physics: Conference Series 142, 012003.
sources.access: Full text read by a verification agent.
sources.use: Minimum ignition energy 0.017 mJ at 22-26% hydrogen in dry air; roughly constant from 10% to 50% at a 2 mm gap; humidity raises it by several tens of percent.
sources.limit: 1 L chamber, 1 atm, room temperature, capacitive sparks.

sources.citation: Soleimani nia, M., Maxwell, B., Oshkai, P. and Djilali, N. (2020). Measurements of flow velocity and scalar concentration in turbulent multi-component jets: asymmetry and buoyancy effects. Experiments in Fluids (arXiv:1811.05580).
sources.access: arXiv full text read on 2026-10-09 (Table 2, Eqs. 4.2-4.4).
sources.use: Centreline mass-fraction decay Y_j/Y_c = C_Y (X - X0)/D_ef with D_ef = D (rho_j/rho_inf)^0.5; C_Y = 0.208 for an H2 pipe jet (Schefer et al. 2008b), 0.21-0.27 for helium round jets, 0.31-0.33 for jets from an orifice in the side of a tube.
sources.limit: Momentum-dominated jets; low-pressure releases become buoyant plumes. The arXiv version was read; volume and article number not recorded.

sources.citation: Schefer, R. W., Houf, W. G. and Williams, T. C. (2008). International Journal of Hydrogen Energy 33(21), 6373-6384 (title not recorded here).
sources.access: Abstract read by a verification agent; its decay constant used as tabulated by Soleimani nia et al. (2020).
sources.use: Hydrogen centreline decay follows the scaling of other variable-density jets.
sources.limit: Constant read from the tabulation, not from the paper.

sources.citation: Bernardy et al. (2025). Journal of Loss Prevention in the Process Industries 94, 105491.
sources.access: Full text read by a verification agent.
sources.use: Summarises the literature range of hydrogen flame radiant fractions as 0.03-0.16.
sources.limit: Review; author list beyond the first author and the title not recorded here. Molina, Schefer and Houf (2007, Proc. Combust. Inst. 31, 2565-2572) was not read.
